questions.q: A production RDS for MySQL instance must survive an AZ failure with automatic failover. The standby does not need to serve reads. Which setup is the simplest?

options.t: Create a read replica in another AZ
options.why: Wrong: replicas use asynchronous replication and are not an automatic failover mechanism for the instance deployment.

options.t: Enable automated backups with 35-day retention
options.why: Wrong: backups help recovery, but restoring takes minutes to hours and is not automatic failover.

options.t: Enable a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment
options.why: Right: one synchronous standby in another AZ; RDS flips the endpoint DNS on failure.

options.t: Move storage to io2 Block Express
options.why: Wrong: faster storage does nothing for AZ failure.

questions.explain: Multi-AZ instance = synchronous standby for HA only.
questions.remember: HA for an RDS instance = Multi-AZ (synchronous standby, same endpoint, no reads). Read replicas, backups and faster storage are different problems.
variants: Readable standbys plus faster failover on RDS MySQL/PostgreSQL → Multi-AZ DB cluster.
Aurora → add an Aurora Replica in another AZ.
Need more read capacity only → read replicas.

questions.q: A team wants an RDS for PostgreSQL deployment where standbys can also serve read traffic and write latency is lower than classic Multi-AZ. Which option fits?

options.t: Multi-AZ DB instance deployment
options.why: Wrong: its single standby is synchronous and cannot serve reads.

options.t: A cross-Region read replica
options.why: Wrong: asynchronous and not a standby in the same Region for failover.

options.t: Aurora Serverless v1
options.why: Wrong: deprecated and a different architecture, not an RDS deployment option.

options.t: Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment
options.why: Right: one writer and two readable standbys in three AZs with semisynchronous replication.

questions.explain: Multi-AZ DB cluster has two readable standbys.
questions.remember: Multi-AZ DB cluster (MySQL/PostgreSQL) = writer + 2 readable standbys, semisynchronous, only on certain instance classes. Multi-AZ instance standby is not readable.
variants: One non-readable standby, synchronous → Multi-AZ DB instance.
Up to 15 readers in an Aurora cluster → Aurora Replicas.
Multi-AZ cluster failover slow → check replica lag.

questions.q: A company needs cross-Region disaster recovery for a database with RPO of about 1 second and RTO of about 1 minute. Which solution fits?

options.t: Cross-Region snapshot copies
options.why: Wrong: RPO is minutes to hours and RTO is hours.

options.t: RDS Multi-AZ instance deployment
options.why: Wrong: protects against AZ failure only, not a Region failure.

options.t: Aurora Global Database
options.why: Right: storage-based replication with lag usually under 1 second and managed failover in about a minute.

options.t: RDS cross-Region read replica promoted manually
options.why: Wrong: RPO equals replica lag and recovery is manual, so RTO is minutes.

questions.explain: Aurora Global Database targets RPO ~1 s and RTO ~1 min.
questions.remember: Region-level DR with ~1 s RPO and ~1 min RTO → Aurora Global Database (up to 10 secondary Regions). Cheaper options: cross-Region replica (pilot light) or snapshot copy.
variants: Hours of RTO at the lowest cost → cross-Region snapshot copy or cross-Region automated backups.
Pilot light on RDS → cross-Region read replica, promote on disaster.
Need to use Backtrack with it → not supported on Global Database.

questions.q: A bad `DELETE` ran 15 minutes ago on an Aurora MySQL cluster. Backtrack was enabled when the cluster was created. What is the fastest recovery?

options.t: Restore a snapshot into a new cluster
options.why: Wrong: slow and creates a new cluster with a new endpoint.

options.t: Promote an Aurora Replica
options.why: Wrong: the replica shares the same volume, so it already has the bad delete.

options.t: Enable Backtrack now and rewind
options.why: Wrong: Backtrack must be enabled at create or restore; it cannot be turned on later.

options.t: Backtrack the cluster to before the delete
options.why: Right: rewinds the cluster in place in minutes, up to 72 hours.

questions.explain: Backtrack rewinds in place; only for Aurora MySQL.
questions.remember: Backtrack = in-place rewind (Aurora MySQL only, enabled at create/restore, up to 72 h, whole cluster). Without it, use PITR to a new cluster. Replicas are not a backup.
variants: Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS → PITR to a new DB, then copy rows back.
Cluster is in a Global Database → Backtrack not supported; use PITR.
Only one table needed → PITR to a new DB and export that table.

questions.q: A developer asks for a full copy of a 2 TB Aurora production cluster for testing within minutes and with very little extra storage cost. What should you do?

options.t: Create an Aurora fast database clone
options.why: Right: copy-on-write at the storage layer; the clone stores only changes.

options.t: Restore the latest automated backup
options.why: Wrong: creates a full copy, takes much longer and costs more storage.

options.t: Create a cross-Region Aurora Global Database
options.why: Wrong: adds replication cost and is meant for DR, not test copies.

options.t: Export a snapshot to S3 in Parquet
options.why: Wrong: exported data cannot be restored into RDS.

questions.explain: Aurora cloning is copy-on-write.
questions.remember: Fast test copy of Aurora data → clone (same Region, up to 15 copy-on-write clones, can share cross-account with RAM).
variants: Need a copy in another Region → snapshot copy or Global Database, not clone.
Need to undo a mistake → Backtrack or PITR, not clone.
16th clone → it is a full copy.

questions.q: An unencrypted RDS instance must be encrypted with a customer managed KMS key. What is the process?

options.t: Modify the instance and enable encryption
options.why: Wrong: encryption can only be enabled at creation.

options.t: Create an encrypted read replica of the instance
options.why: Wrong: an encrypted replica of an unencrypted source is not allowed.

options.t: Snapshot, copy the snapshot with encryption on, restore, then cut over
options.why: Right: encryption is applied during the snapshot copy.

options.t: Enable TDE on the instance
options.why: Wrong: TDE exists only for Oracle and SQL Server and is separate from RDS encryption.

questions.explain: You encrypt during the snapshot copy.
questions.remember: Existing unencrypted DB → snapshot → encrypted copy → restore → switch endpoint. You can neither add nor remove encryption in place, nor change its KMS key.
variants: Change KMS key of an encrypted DB → copy a snapshot with the new key and restore.
Share snapshot with another account → needs a customer managed key shared with that account.
Require encryption for all new DBs → AWS Config rule or SCP.

questions.q: A compliance team must stop engineers from creating RDS read replicas or snapshot copies in unapproved Regions across all accounts. Which control is best?

options.t: A security group on each database
options.why: Wrong: security groups filter network traffic, not API actions.

options.t: An SCP that denies `rds:CopyDBSnapshot` and `rds:CreateDBInstanceReadReplica` outside approved Regions
options.why: Right: controls the API actions centrally across accounts.

options.t: Enable Multi-AZ
options.why: Wrong: an HA setting; it does not restrict Regions.

options.t: Turn on Performance Insights
options.why: Wrong: a monitoring feature, not a preventive control.

questions.explain: Use IAM/SCP and Region restrictions.
questions.remember: Data sovereignty on RDS = deny cross-Region replica and snapshot copy actions with IAM policies or SCPs plus Region restrictions.
variants: Detect rather than prevent → AWS Config rules.
Who made the change → CloudTrail.
Prevent S3 replication to other Regions → bucket policy/SCP on S3 actions.

questions.q: Thousands of short-lived Lambda invocations open connections to an Aurora MySQL database and cause `too many connections` errors. The database is in a private subnet. What reduces the problem with the least code change?

options.t: Increase the Lambda memory
options.why: Wrong: does not change how many DB connections are opened.

options.t: Add more Aurora Replicas
options.why: Wrong: readers do not raise the writer connection limit.

options.t: Make the database publicly accessible
options.why: Wrong: does not fix the connection storm and adds exposure.

options.t: Put RDS Proxy in front of the database
options.why: Right: it pools and multiplexes client connections over fewer DB connections.

questions.explain: RDS Proxy absorbs connection storms.
questions.remember: Many short connections (Lambda, microservices) → RDS Proxy. It also speeds failover and supports IAM auth plus Secrets Manager. Pinning disables multiplexing.
variants: Lambda outside a VPC with no connections to manage → Aurora Data API.
Proxy does not reduce DB connections → sessions are pinned (SET variables, temp tables, large statements).
Need the proxy reachable from the internet → not possible; it is VPC-only.

questions.q: A Lambda function outside any VPC needs to run SQL against an Aurora cluster without managing connections or VPC configuration. Which feature fits?

options.t: RDS Proxy
options.why: Wrong: it is VPC-only, so the caller must be inside the VPC.

options.t: IAM database authentication alone
options.why: Wrong: it still needs a network path and a native connection.

options.t: Database Activity Streams
options.why: Wrong: an auditing feature, not a query path.

options.t: Aurora Data API
options.why: Right: an HTTPS SQL endpoint using IAM and a Secrets Manager secret, with no persistent connections.

questions.explain: Data API = HTTPS SQL for Aurora.
questions.remember: No VPC, no connection management, Aurora → Data API (limits: 4 MB request, 1 MB result set, 10 MB JSON response). Not for high-throughput transactional loops.
variants: Data API result over 1 MB → paginate or use a native connection.
Lambda inside the VPC with heavy traffic → RDS Proxy.
Plain RDS (non-Aurora) instance → Data API is Aurora-only.

questions.q: An application stores RDS database passwords in code. The security team wants credentials rotated automatically with no application downtime. What should you do?

options.t: Rotate the master password manually each quarter
options.why: Wrong: manual and error-prone, and the app still holds the password.

options.t: Store the password in an AMI
options.why: Wrong: embedding secrets in images is explicitly discouraged.

options.t: Store the credentials in Secrets Manager with alternating-users rotation
options.why: Right: rotation uses a Lambda function and one user stays valid during the change, so there is no downtime.

options.t: Use CloudTrail to detect password age
options.why: Wrong: CloudTrail does not rotate anything.

questions.explain: Secrets Manager rotation, alternating users for zero downtime.
questions.remember: Credentials rotation for RDS → Secrets Manager (Lambda-based, built-in templates). Alternating-users avoids downtime. RDS can also manage and rotate the master password.
variants: No passwords at all for MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL → IAM database authentication (15-minute token, TLS required).
High connection churn with IAM auth → RDS Proxy.
Rotation fails when adding a Region to Aurora Global Database → turn the managed master password off first.

questions.q: An application on EC2 should connect to RDS for PostgreSQL without any stored password. Which statements are correct? (Choose 2)

options.t: Call `generate-db-auth-token` and use the token as the password
options.why: Right: the signed token lasts 15 minutes.

options.t: Grant `rds:connect` on the instance ARN
options.why: Wrong: the action is `rds-db:connect` on a dbuser resource ARN.

options.t: Connect over SSL/TLS and grant the `rds_iam` role to the database user
options.why: Right: IAM authentication requires TLS and the PostgreSQL role mapping.

options.t: The token never expires
options.why: Wrong: tokens expire after 15 minutes.

options.t: CloudTrail logs every token generation
options.why: Wrong: token generation is not logged by CloudTrail.

questions.explain: IAM DB auth = 15-minute token, TLS, rds-db:connect.
questions.remember: IAM database authentication works for MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL. Token lasts 15 minutes, TLS is required, policy uses `rds-db:connect`. PostgreSQL users need `rds_iam`.
variants: IAM auth fails after a few minutes → token expired; generate a new one.
Many new connections per second → use RDS Proxy.
Oracle or SQL Server → not supported; use Secrets Manager or Kerberos.

questions.q: Analysts need to query an RDS for PostgreSQL table but must not see raw PII columns. Which statement about RDS is accurate?

options.t: RDS has a built-in managed masking feature to enable
options.why: Wrong: RDS has no managed masking.

options.t: Macie scans RDS tables directly
options.why: Wrong: Macie only scans S3.

options.t: Use masking views or app-layer tokenization, or move data to a lake or warehouse and apply column controls there
options.why: Right: RDS has no managed masking, so you build it with views/extensions or downstream controls.

options.t: Enable TDE to hide columns from analysts
options.why: Wrong: TDE encrypts storage and is transparent to authorized users.

questions.explain: No managed masking in RDS.
questions.remember: RDS/Aurora have no managed masking: use views, extensions, tokenization, or replicate to Redshift/Lake Formation for column and row controls. Macie scans only S3 (use it on exports).
variants: Per-tenant row filtering in PostgreSQL → row-level security policies.
Find PII in exported snapshots → Macie on the S3 export.
Mask while moving data downstream → Glue sensitive-data detection or DataBrew.

questions.q: A company wants to migrate an on-premises Oracle database to Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime. Which combination is correct?

options.t: DMS alone, since it converts all schema and code
options.why: Wrong: DMS moves data; schema and code conversion needs SCT or DMS Schema Conversion.

options.t: A snapshot restore of the Oracle backup
options.why: Wrong: a heterogeneous migration cannot restore across engines.

options.t: An Aurora cross-Region replica
options.why: Wrong: replicas only exist within the same engine family.

options.t: SCT or DMS Schema Conversion for schema and code, then DMS full load plus CDC
options.why: Right: converts the schema, loads data, then streams changes until cut-over.

questions.explain: Heterogeneous migration = SCT + DMS (full load + CDC).
questions.remember: Changing engine → SCT/DMS Schema Conversion for schema, DMS for data (full load + CDC). Same engine → native tools or snapshots.
variants: DMS source on PostgreSQL → set `rds.logical_replication=1`.
DMS source on MySQL → `binlog_format=ROW` and retain binary logs.
Oracle source CDC → supplemental logging.

questions.q: Analysts want near-real-time analytics on Aurora MySQL data in Amazon Redshift without building or maintaining a pipeline. Both are in the same Region. What is best?

options.t: Nightly snapshot export to S3 plus a COPY job
options.why: Wrong: batch-oriented and it needs a pipeline.

options.t: Redshift federated query only
options.why: Wrong: queries the live database and adds load, instead of replicating data.

options.t: An Aurora zero-ETL integration with Redshift
options.why: Right: near-real-time replication with no pipeline to build.

options.t: A Glue crawler over the cluster
options.why: Wrong: a crawler catalogs tables but does not replicate data continuously.

questions.explain: Zero-ETL = near-real-time, no pipeline.
questions.remember: OLTP → Redshift continuously without pipeline code → zero-ETL (same Region, PK needed on Aurora PostgreSQL tables, max 5 integrations per source). One-off or batch lake load → snapshot export to S3 (Parquet).
variants: A zero-ETL table is failed on Aurora PostgreSQL → likely no primary key.
Lake needs a cheap one-off copy → snapshot export to S3 plus Athena.
Per-query access to live data → federated query.

questions.q: A RAG application stores embeddings in Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector. The table is large and queries are slow. Developers want the fastest queries with high recall and can afford memory; the table is built up as data arrives. Which index?

options.t: IVFFlat created on the empty table
options.why: Wrong: it needs data first to compute its clusters.

options.t: HNSW with an operator class matching the distance, for example `vector_cosine_ops`
options.why: Right: graph-based approximate search, fast with high recall, no training, and it can start empty.

options.t: No index
options.why: Wrong: exact search scans the whole table; slow on large data.

options.t: A B-tree index on the vector column
options.why: Wrong: B-tree cannot do similarity search.

questions.explain: HNSW = speed and recall; IVFFlat = cheaper builds.
questions.remember: pgvector: HNSW for best speed/recall and updates as data arrives (more memory, slower build). IVFFlat for cheaper, faster builds on large data but build after loading data. No index = exact search for small tables.
variants: Memory constrained, big data, fast build → IVFFlat (build after data is loaded).
Must have 100% recall on a small table → no ANN index.
Build fails or is slow → raise `maintenance_work_mem`.

questions.q: A team wants Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases to use Aurora PostgreSQL as the vector store. Which prerequisites are required? (Choose 2)

options.t: pgvector 0.5.0 or later with a `vector(n)` column matching the embedding model dimension
options.why: Right: the table needs an embedding column and an HNSW cosine index.

options.t: Aurora Serverless v1
options.why: Wrong: it is deprecated and not the stated requirement.

options.t: RDS Data API enabled and a Secrets Manager secret
options.why: Right: Bedrock accesses the database through the Data API with credentials in Secrets Manager.

options.t: Aurora MySQL with Backtrack
options.why: Wrong: the vector store needs PostgreSQL with pgvector.

options.t: A public endpoint on the cluster
options.why: Wrong: not required; the Data API handles access.

questions.explain: Bedrock KB on Aurora = pgvector + Data API + secret.
questions.remember: Aurora PostgreSQL as a Bedrock KB vector store: supported version, pgvector 0.5.0+, Data API enabled, Secrets Manager secret, table with id/embedding/chunks/metadata and HNSW index. Dimension must match the model (for example 1024).
variants: Large-scale hybrid text and vector search → OpenSearch.
Ultra-low-latency vector search → MemoryDB.
SQL filters, joins and transactions with vectors → Aurora/RDS PostgreSQL pgvector.

questions.q: On RDS for PostgreSQL, all application requests suddenly hang. Investigation suggests one session holds locks and blocks others. How do you find and end the blocker?

options.t: Query `SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS` and run `CALL mysql.rds_kill`
options.why: Wrong: these are MySQL/InnoDB tools.

options.t: Check `pg_stat_activity` and `pg_blocking_pids()`, then run `pg_terminate_backend(pid)`
options.why: Right: the PostgreSQL way to find and end a blocker.

options.t: Reboot with failover
options.why: Wrong: a drastic step that does not fix the application's transaction handling.

options.t: Create a read replica
options.why: Wrong: replicas do not release locks on the primary.

questions.explain: Use engine-specific lock views.
questions.remember: Blocked sessions: PostgreSQL `pg_stat_activity`/`pg_locks`/`pg_blocking_pids()`; MySQL `innodb_trx`, `rds_kill`; SQL Server `sys.dm_tran_locks`; Oracle `V$LOCK`. Prevent with short transactions and timeouts.
variants: MySQL blocker → `information_schema.innodb_trx`, then `mysql.rds_kill`.
Deadlock → engine kills a victim; the app must retry.
Idle-in-transaction sessions → set `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout`.

questions.q: An Aurora cluster's bill shows I/O charges at 40% of the total. The workload is steady and I/O heavy. What is the best change?

options.t: Switch to Aurora Serverless v2
options.why: Wrong: pays per ACU but does not remove per-I/O charges.

options.t: Add more Aurora Replicas
options.why: Wrong: readers add instance cost and I/O is counted on readers too.

options.t: Switch the cluster to Aurora I/O-Optimized
options.why: Right: no per-I/O charges; best when I/O is 25% or more of the bill.

options.t: Move to gp3 storage
options.why: Wrong: Aurora uses its own cluster volume, not gp3.

questions.explain: I/O at 25% of bill or more → I/O-Optimized.
questions.remember: Aurora Standard = storage + per-million I/O; I/O-Optimized = no I/O charge but higher instance and storage price. Choose by the 25% rule. Standard → I/O-Optimized once per 30 days; back to Standard any time.
variants: I/O under about 25% of the bill → stay on Standard.
Plain RDS needs predictable high IOPS → io2 Block Express.
Switched to I/O-Optimized yesterday and want to switch again → Standard→I/O-Optimized limited to once per 30 days; switching back is allowed.

questions.q: A SaaS company has spiky and unpredictable Aurora MySQL traffic and dev environments that sit idle overnight. They want cost to follow usage. Which option fits?

options.t: A large provisioned writer with Reserved Instances
options.why: Wrong: good for steady 24/7 load, wasteful for spiky load.

options.t: Aurora Serverless v1
options.why: Wrong: deprecated; use v2.

options.t: RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster
options.why: Wrong: fixed capacity, not usage-based.

options.t: Aurora Serverless v2, with min 0 ACU auto-pause for dev
options.why: Right: scales in 0.5 ACU steps without disrupting connections; at 0 ACU only storage is billed.

questions.explain: Serverless v2 for spiky or idle workloads.
questions.remember: Serverless v2: min/max ACU, per-second billing, auto-pause at 0 ACU for idle dev. Steady heavy 24/7 load is cheaper on provisioned plus Reserved Instances. Keep min ACU high enough to keep the cache warm.
variants: Steady 24/7 heavy load → provisioned with Reserved Instances.
Readers should be ready for failover → promotion tier 0–1 keep capacity at least the writer's.
RDS (non-Aurora) dev instance idle at night → stop it (up to 7 days).

questions.q: A major MySQL version upgrade on RDS must cause minimal downtime, and the team wants to test first and be able to roll back. What should they use?

options.t: Modify the instance directly in the maintenance window
options.why: Wrong: may need significant downtime and has no staging environment.

options.t: Create a read replica and promote it after upgrade
options.why: Wrong: not a managed test-and-switch workflow.

options.t: Enable RDS Extended Support
options.why: Wrong: it keeps an old version running for a fee; it does not upgrade.

options.t: Blue/Green Deployments
options.why: Right: copies production to a synchronized green environment, upgrade and test there, then switch over, typically in under a minute.

questions.explain: Blue/Green = upgrade in staging, switch over.
questions.remember: Low-downtime major upgrade or schema/parameter change → Blue/Green Deployments (MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Aurora). Keep the old blue for rollback. Extended Support only delays the upgrade, for a per-vCPU-hour fee.
variants: Cannot upgrade MySQL 5.7 yet → RDS Extended Support as a paid bridge (up to 3 years).
Minor version upgrade → maintenance window or auto minor upgrade.
Zero-ETL source during switchover → delete integration first, recreate afterwards.

questions.q: An RDS for PostgreSQL instance has `storage-full` events every few months because data growth is unpredictable. The team cannot shrink the volume later but wants to avoid outages. What should they do?

options.t: Enable storage autoscaling with a maximum storage threshold
options.why: Right: RDS grows storage automatically when space is low; it never shrinks.

options.t: Switch to magnetic storage
options.why: Wrong: magnetic is deprecated and does not support autoscaling.

options.t: Take a snapshot daily
options.why: Wrong: backups do not add free space.

options.t: Add a read replica
options.why: Wrong: a replica does not increase source storage.

questions.explain: Storage autoscaling with a max threshold.
questions.remember: RDS storage grows (autoscaling or manual) but cannot shrink in place; to shrink, migrate to a smaller new instance. Aurora grows automatically. WAL or replication slots can also fill the disk.
variants: Aurora → storage grows automatically; no autoscaling setting.
Disk full because of WAL → find a lagging or unused replication slot and drop it.
Need to shrink storage → dump/restore or DMS to a new instance.

questions.q: An RDS for MySQL source has automated backups and several read replicas. A KMS key used to encrypt the source is disabled by mistake and the instance becomes `inaccessible-encryption-credentials-recoverable`. What is correct?

options.t: The instance is gone; only a PITR can help
options.why: Wrong: not yet: it is recoverable for a limited time.

options.t: Changing the instance class restores access
options.why: Wrong: the problem is the key, not compute.

options.t: Re-enable the key and start the instance within 7 days, or restore from the final snapshot
options.why: Right: the instance is stopped and recoverable for up to 7 days; after that the state is terminal.

options.t: Create an unencrypted replica to bypass the key
options.why: Wrong: mixing encrypted and unencrypted is not allowed.

questions.explain: Re-enable the KMS key within 7 days.
questions.remember: Disabled or deleted KMS key → `inaccessible-encryption-credentials-recoverable` (up to 7 days to re-enable and start), then terminal `inaccessible-encryption-credentials` (restore from snapshot). Revoking a user's key access does not affect a running DB.
variants: Replicas must use the same KMS key in the same Region as the source.
Cross-Region replica → key from the destination Region.
Accidentally set retention to 0 on RDS → PITR is impossible.
